title: How many sets per muscle do you actually need each week?
hook: How many sets per muscle do you actually need each week?
caption:
How many sets per muscle do you actually need each week?

The honest answer is not one magic number.

Higher weekly training volume can support more muscle growth, but the return from each additional set becomes smaller while fatigue continues to accumulate. Your useful dose also depends on training experience, exercise selection, effort, recovery and how much indirect work a muscle receives.

Start by counting meaningful working sets — not warm-ups or effortless reps. Keep the lowest volume that still allows you to improve repetitions, load or execution over several weeks.

title: Everyone’s chasing progressive overload and trying to destroy the muscle. But if you wreck it, it’s often still beat up by the next time you train it. 💥
hook: Everyone’s chasing progressive overload and trying to destroy the muscle. But if you wreck it, it’s often still beat up by the next time you train it. 💥
caption:
Everyone’s chasing progressive overload and trying to destroy the muscle. But if you wreck it, it’s often still beat up by the next time you train it. 💥

Enter reverse drop sets. Start with a weight that’s heavy enough to count, and get your cleanest, best-quality reps in first. Don’t burn out. Then add weight and keep going until you hit the “growth rep,” the hard rep the whole set was building toward.

When you get stuck, that’s your weak spot. Don’t run from it. Hang out there. That’s the part that needs the work to make the whole lift stronger. 💪

title: Nobody tells you why they said no.
hook: Nobody tells you why they said no.
caption:
Nobody tells you why they said no.

They go quiet. They close the tab. They say "let me think about it."

But the doubt behind it is almost always one of seven.

Is this for me?
Do you get my situation?
Who else has done this?
How does it work?
How long will it take?
What if it fails?
What happens next?

Most pages answer none of them. So the visitor fills the gap with the worst guess.

This week, read your page as a stranger. Find the doubt you never answer. Then answer it right where it shows up.

Save this for your next page review.

Incline Press - Felt better on the shoulder when focusing more on the elbows out and elbows in cue. Helps you stop the ROM in a more natural plane without stressing the shoulder too much.

Back Work - Pull ups felt strong. Close to a +1 here. For rows, video is important. Thought I was losing too much ROM with the last rep but could have gone for 1 or 2 more. 

Arm Work - Preachers were good. Top set and back off set feel better rather than grinding in the 2-4 rep range. PR on pushdowns. Pausing at the bottom is helping a lot to make the rep smoother.
